# DAAF — Data Analyst Augmentation Framework (Brian Heseung Kim)

license: `LGPL-3.0-or-later (as declared in the README, badge and CITATION.cff; the repo ships the GPL-3.0 text as LICENSE plus COPYING.LESSER)` · 56 skills · last update: 2026-08-18

**Source:** <https://github.com/DAAF-Contribution-Community/daaf>

**Maintainers:** Brian Heseung Kim (brhkim on GitHub), for the DAAF-Contribution-Community organisation

**Compatibility:** `claude-code`

> DAAF is a Claude Code instruction framework, run inside a Docker container, that turns the agent into a file-first quantitative research assistant: every data step is a script on disk, a 15-agent roster works under an orchestrator skill, and the analysis runs through a staged pipeline whose Stage 9 archives the executed scripts into marimo (Python) or Quarto (R) notebooks. All 56 SKILL.md files under .claude/skills/ are catalogued here. A provenance audit (md5 plus difflib word-sequence ratio, 2026-09-29) against every details copy RISE already holds, against K-Dense-AI/claude-scientific-skills, anthropics/skills, meleantonio/awesome-econ-ai-stuff, hanlulong/econ-paper-review-skill, JonasWeinert/EconAgentSkills and pedrohcgs/claude-code-my-workflow, and against the 69 other repos in the Auto-Empirical-Research-Skills bundle finds no vendored copies: the best external match is 0.077 (DAAF polars against K-Dense polars), and the library skills that share names with K-Dense skills (polars, scikit-learn, statsmodels, geopandas, plotly) are independent rewrites. The skills fall into five groups: framework internals (orchestrator, agent and skill authoring, shell scripting, deployment smoke tests, web retrieval), method routing (data-scientist, creative-verification, synthetic-data-workflow, science-communication), paired Python and R library skills (pyfixest and fixest, statsmodels and r-stats, linearmodels and plm, svy and survey-r, scikit-learn and tidymodels, geopandas and sf-terra, igraph and igraph-r, plotnine and ggplot2, plotly and plotly-r, great-tables and gt, polars and tidyverse, marimo and quarto), four Stata, R and Python translation skills, and 17 data-source skills, 16 of them for the Urban Institute Education Data Portal and its mirror (CCD, IPEDS, CRDC, Scorecard, EDFacts and others) plus MIT MEDSL county presidential returns. The education-data focus reflects the project's proof of concept; the method skills are domain-general. Several skills are framework plumbing rather than research guidance (daaf-orchestrator is loaded only by the orchestrator, daaf-deploy-smoke-testing needs the DAAF_DEV=1 dev image). The details copies are verbatim and are redistributed under LGPL-3.0-or-later with attribution to Brian Heseung Kim and the DAAF contributors; each upstream skill also ships reference files that are not copied here.


**Source YAML:** [`skills/daaf.yml`](https://github.com/bhanneke/RISE/blob/main/skills/daaf.yml)
